alternative_explanations_tested.evidence_for: sub-pockets exist: an 8-wallet family in h11 (root 57707.eth 0x29a303c3; 07212/05323/07176/07121/06632/05605/16568.eth; first-funder links among them date to 2022; each received 0.09993 ETH from a Binance hot wallet 07:07-07:18 UTC 2026-08-17 then deposited 0.1 in h11) => plausibly ONE owner with 8 aged wallets (caught by peel-chain, not by the window); 6 nonce-0 wallets of which >=3 are 3-4-tx burners; a 2-wallet pair (0x0e2e8cae/0x5927d281) with identical tx history

alternative_explanations_tested.evidence: only 6/113 first-funded by ChainCred infra CEX wallets and 22/113 by exchange-scale EOAs (0xa7efae72 x4, 0x9696f59e x3, 0xbf94f0ac x3, 0x623777cc x3, Binance16 x3 ...); 75/113 funded by ordinary addresses; exchange funding is not evidence either way

alternative_explanations_tested.hypothesis: they would be released by the suggested fix (no weld from windows >2h)
alternative_explanations_tested.evidence: detaching A (dropping the 5 crossing tier-A edges) still leaves A as its own 113-member cluster (families amount+funding, conf 0.99) via round-wave x113 + exchange hubs (x2-x4) + the h11 peel chain; capping round windows at 2h still flags 79/113 (15 in the big cluster, 31 in a 52-cluster, 11+22 in own clusters); only the wallet-level rule (nonce>=20 & no strong rule => no edge) releases them: 74/113 qualify
alternative_explanations_tested.verdict: the mechanism claim inside c6 holds; the fix as stated is insufficient
